title: api-gateway: routing rules, payload limits, and streaming proxy buffer tweaks for OpenAI-compat surface stability
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed increased error rates and partial-stream truncation for clients using the OpenAI compatibility layer when gateway routing switched backends or when large tool-calling payloads traversed the streaming proxy. This changeset tightens routing rules, adds defensive payload-size limits and soft-fail fallbacks, and increases/clarifies streaming proxy buffer handling to improve stability without changing public API semantics. Summary of changes: 1) Router: added explicit route affinity rules so OpenAI-compat requests are pinned to backends supporting streaming + function/tool calling; new route annotations allow per-customer overrides via routing policy. 2) Payload limits: introduce per-route and per-model configurable payload limits (default 1.5MB request body, 10MB aggregate multipart/tool payload) with structured error responses conforming to OpenAI-compat error codes for easy client handling. 3) Streaming proxy: increased in-memory buffer thresholds, added chunked-forwarding logic to avoid head-of-line blocking, and implemented a backpressure signal to the runtime when proxy buffers reach 80% capacity. 4) Compatibility adapter: openai-compat adapter now tags streaming requests and preserves function_call/structured_output hints during routing and fallback. 5) Observability: new metrics (gateway.route_affinity, proxy.buffer_fill_pct, compat.fallback_count) and tracing annotations added. 6) Tests: integration tests for streaming proxy under route failover, unit tests for payload limit enforcement and compat adapter behavior. Rollout plan: feature gated by gateway.flag.streaming_stability and will be enabled for a small percentage of traffic for 48h before ramp. Migration notes: admins can set per-customer routing policies or adjust payload thresholds; default behavior preserves existing API semantics except for explicit 413-like responses when payloads exceed limits. See release_notes and docs for guidance.

release_notes:
- API gateway: improved stability for streaming requests and OpenAI-compat tool/function calling under backend failover.
- New configurable per-route and per-model payload limits with OpenAI-style 413 responses.
- Streaming proxy: reduced chance of partial stream truncation by chunked-forwarding and backpressure signaling.
- New observability metrics: gateway.route_affinity, proxy.buffer_fill_pct, compat.fallback_count.
Admins: enable gateway.flag.streaming_stability and monitor proxy.buffer_fill_pct during rollout. Adjust per-customer routing_policy and payload thresholds if needed.
notes_for_ops: Gate behind gateway.flag.streaming_stability; start at 2% traffic, monitor proxy.buffer_fill_pct and compat.fallback_count for 48h; in case of elevated 413s, increase per-route limits or consult customer routing_policy; rollback by disabling flag or reverting to previous router policy config.
additional_context: This change is targeted at reducing incidents where long-running streaming requests were cut off during backend routing changes and when large tool-call payloads caused the streaming proxy to buffer excessively. The solution keeps API compatibility while making internal routing decisions more explicit and observable.
